cuOpt watchdog settings

Source: R/cuopt_watchdog.R
cuopt_watchdog.Rd

Thresholds for stopping a cuOpt (PDLP) solve that diverges or stalls. The watchdog reads cuopt_cli's iteration log every poll seconds and stops the solve when

  • runaway: the primal or dual objective stays beyond runaway in absolute value for runaway_n consecutive log lines (cuOpt logs every 1,000 iterations), or

  • stall: over the last stall_window seconds, or the last stall_iter iterations, none of the primal residual, the dual residual and the gap improved on its best value before that window by a factor stall_factor.

Usage

cuopt_watchdog(
  poll = 30,
  runaway = 1e+20,
  runaway_n = 5,
  stall_window = 1800,
  stall_iter = 5e+05,
  stall_factor = 2
)

Arguments

poll

seconds between log reads.

runaway, runaway_n

the runaway rule.

stall_window, stall_iter, stall_factor

the stall rule.

Value

a cuopt_watchdog list.

Details

A rule whose threshold is NA is off. Pass FALSE as control$watchdog (or the session option) to turn the watchdog off; it also stays off when the 'processx' package is not installed.

Precedence: control$watchdog of the solve, then getOption("multimod.cuopt_watchdog"), then cuopt_watchdog().

Examples

cuopt_watchdog()
#> <cuopt_watchdog>
#>   poll          30
#>   runaway       1e+20
#>   runaway_n     5
#>   stall_window  1800
#>   stall_iter    5e+05
#>   stall_factor  2
# a longer stall window for a slow but healthy model
w <- cuopt_watchdog(stall_window = 3600)
# control$watchdog <- w   (or FALSE to turn it off)
